reviewer.note: Round 2 of 3 (PR #513, head d13494db, sha256 34cc6a9d). The round-1 faults are fixed. At 1x and 2x beside Bramble the climb reads as a timber stair up the cliff, and the cheeks and kerbs read as dressed stone edging, not rails. Measured: a 15-row pitch with 5 steps (y 766-840); stair_read riser shares are 0.33/0.40/0.40/0.40/0.40 (median 0.40), and the detector passes. Each riser has 4 tones plus a 1% fifth, the largest covering 0.35-0.39. Steps 2-5 differ from step 1 in 179-234 of 825 texels. The stringers are notched, the contact row at y 841 is L 61/91, and the west kerb shades the landing. bands.score: stair wood (356-410 x 766-840) 0.907 against prop; whole stair 1.081 prop and 0.897 stone. The cheeks were measured with same-area sliding windows (10x32 and 7x46). That window shape changes nothing on the approved rock (10x32 gives 39.8 shapes, 18x18 gives 40.4), so the cheeks' score is not a patch-size artefact. The west cheek scores 0.82 tones and 1.00 shapes; the east cheek 0.69 and 0.73, which is a real shortfall but above the approved rock face beside it (0.64-0.66). Polish, which does not block placement: (a) on steps 1-4 the riser's bottom row is L 121, almost the tread's L 130, over a dark back row on the tread (L 46/75), so the joint has a lit lip where it should be occluded; this came from the round-1 fix note. Move the light to the tread's back row, end the riser at 70-96, and aim for a riser share of 0.43-0.53 (Eastward). (b) The pegs sit in the same 4 columns (359-360, 363-364, 403-404, 407-408) on every tread; shift some by 1-2 px. (c) Give the east cheek more chips and pits. Above row 760 only 25 texels differ from main. The detectors' status is left as written (0 findings).
